summary: AI coding tools have become ubiquitous in 2026, with JetBrains research reporting 90% weekly and 68% daily use among professional developers. The landscape is dominated by GitHub Copilot (the enterprise default with 20M+ users), Cursor (the favored AI-native IDE), and Claude Code (the terminal-native agent with the highest SWE-bench scores), while agentic autonomous coding tools from OpenAI, Cognition, and cloud vendors round out the field. Model flexibility, agentic autonomy, and deep IDE/CI integration are now the key differentiators.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
strengths: Widest multi-model selector including Opus 5 and Sonnet 5
Agent mode with cloud agents that open PRs
Fits inside existing Microsoft enterprise agreements
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams wanting a pragmatic, broadly-integrated default inside existing Microsoft/GitHub workflows

tools.name: Cursor
strengths: In-editor model switching across multiple providers
Inline diff-based apply with developer approval
Own Composer model plus frontier and Grok models
tools.best_for: Everyday shipping in an AI-native IDE with strong multi-file edits and refactoring

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Claude Pro $20/mo and Max $100-200/mo; API usage-based
strengths: Strongest 'coding brain' for genuinely hard problems
Terminal-native autonomous agent that plans, edits files, and runs shell commands
tools.best_for: Complex, autonomous multi-step coding tasks requiring deep reasoning

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.pricing_paid: Included with ChatGPT Plus $20/mo, Pro $200/mo; API usage-based
tools.best_for: Delegating well-scoped coding tasks to an autonomous cloud agent

tools.name: Amazon Q Developer
strengths: Strong for cloud infrastructure and migrations
tools.best_for: Teams building on AWS needing cloud-aware coding and migration assistance

tools.name: Devin Desktop
strengths: Successor to Windsurf/Codeium with agentic workflows
tools.best_for: Delegating full engineering tasks to a fully autonomous AI engineer

tools.name: JetBrains AI Assistant
strengths: Deep native integration across JetBrains IDEs
tools.best_for: Developers working within the JetBrains IDE ecosystem

tools.name: Google Gemini Code Assist
strengths: Large context window via Gemini models
tools.best_for: Developers in the Google Cloud ecosystem wanting a strong free tier

tools.name: Tabnine
strengths: Code remains private, no training on user code
tools.best_for: Security- and privacy-conscious enterprises needing self-hosted AI coding

tools.name: RooCode
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; pay for model API usage (BYOK)
tools.best_for: Developers wanting an open-source, reliable agent for large-scale code changes
